poin.isi: xAI released Grok 4.7 on September 21 at 2 dollars per million input tokens and 6 dollars per million output tokens — the same price level as its predecessor, and far below top-tier models like GPT-5.6 Sol Max (4/20 dollars) and Fable 5.1 Max (10/50 dollars).

On the independent Artificial Analysis index, Grok 4.7 scores 46, while Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 each score 53. On the agentic coding test Terminal-Bench 4.0 it reaches 26 percent, behind GPT-6 Astra (60 percent) and Fable 5.1 (55 percent).

AI prices are falling, but the cheapest model is not automatically the right one. Match the model to the job: high-volume routine work to efficient models, complex work to the most capable ones. A bad match creates rework.

headline: AI MODEL PRICES KEEP FALLING
CHEAPEST ISN'T ALWAYS RIGHT
headline_caption: xAI releases Grok 4.7: cheap and fast, but not the most capable.
subjudul: More capable models are getting cheaper. What decides the outcome is not the price tag, but the fit with the task.
